hints: Half the chord length is $6$. Use Pythagoras with radius $10$ to find altitude $d = \sqrt{10^2 - 6^2} = \sqrt{64} = 8$.
The area of triangle $CAB$ with base $AB = 12$ and height $d = 8$ is $\dfrac{1}{2} \times 12 \times 8 = 48$.
walkthrough:
Half the chord and its perpendicular height form a right triangle with the radius.
Calculate the altitude $d$ from the centre $C$ to the chord $AB$:
$$d = \sqrt{r^2 - (AB/2)^2} = \sqrt{10^2 - 6^2} = \sqrt{100 - 36} = \sqrt{64} = 8$$

Calculate the area of the isosceles triangle $CAB$:
$$\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times AB \times d = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 12 \times 8 = 48$$
